question: If all the oceans' salt were one cube, how big would it be?
answer: Piling up every grain of salt dissolved in the seas would make a cube about 265 km on each side, roughly as wide as all of Sicily. Standing beside Etna, you would look up at a wall of salt.
move: The oceans hold an island-sized cube of salt: about 265 km a side.
